questions.q: Explain why a computer needs secondary storage as well as RAM.

markPoints.concept: RAM is volatile, so its contents are lost when the power goes
markPoints.exemplar: RAM is volatile, so everything in it is lost when the power goes off.

markPoints.concept: secondary storage is non-volatile, so files are still there next time
markPoints.exemplar: Secondary storage is non-volatile, so files are still there next time.

questions.example: RAM is volatile, so anything in it disappears when the computer is switched off. Secondary storage is non-volatile, so files are still there the next time the computer is used.
questions.paraphrase: Memory empties when the power goes, while a drive keeps what is on it, so work survives being switched off.
questions.feedback: One mark for what RAM cannot do, one for what secondary storage can.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 3 — Storage warehouse, station 1: Why secondary storage?

questions.q: Which is the best description of secondary storage?
options: Non-volatile storage used to keep programs and data when the computer is off
Memory the CPU reads from directly during the cycle
A small amount of very fast memory inside the CPU
Space used only when RAM becomes full
questions.feedback: Virtual memory is one use of secondary storage, not what it is.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 3 — Storage warehouse, station 1: Why secondary storage?

questions.q: Match each storage type to how it stores data.
pairs: Pits and lands burnt into a disc, read by a laser
Charge held in flash memory cells, with no moving parts
questions.feedback: Spin, laser, no moving parts — the three mechanisms.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 3 — Storage warehouse, station 2: Magnetic storage

questions.q: Which part of a hard disk drive moves across the platters to read and write data?
questions.feedback: The spindle spins the platters; the head moves across them. A laser belongs to optical storage.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 3 — Storage warehouse, station 2: Magnetic storage

questions.q: Name one moving part found in a magnetic hard disk drive.

markPoints.concept: a named moving part: the platter, the spindle or the read/write head

questions.feedback: Platters, spindle, arm or head. This is the reason an HDD is more easily damaged by being dropped.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 3 — Storage warehouse, station 2: Magnetic storage

questions.q: Solid state storage has no moving parts.
questions.feedback: True, and it is the reason an SSD is more durable, quieter and faster to access than a hard disk.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 3 — Storage warehouse, station 2: Magnetic storage

questions.q: A school is buying laptops for pupils to carry between lessons. Explain why solid state storage is a better choice than a magnetic hard disk.

accept: no moving parts|without moving parts|nothing moves|solid state|no platters|no spinning|nothing inside to break|nothing to break|nothing moving
markPoints.exemplar: An SSD has no moving parts.

markPoints.concept: so they are far more resistant to being knocked or dropped
accept: durable|robust|resist|survive|withstand|less likely to break|less easily damaged|less likely to be damaged|harder to damage|shock|nothing inside to break|nothing to break
markPoints.exemplar: This means it is much less likely to be damaged if a laptop is dropped.

markPoints.concept: and they are faster to access and use less power, which helps battery life
markPoints.exemplar: They are also faster and use less power.

questions.example: An SSD has no moving parts, so it is far less likely to be damaged when a laptop is carried around and dropped. It is also faster to read and uses less power, which makes the laptop quicker to start and the battery last longer.
questions.paraphrase: There is nothing inside to break if it gets knocked, which matters for something carried about; on top of that it reads more quickly and draws less power.
questions.feedback: Durability is the point of the scenario. The other two marks are the ordinary advantages.
questions.hint: What is different about the inside of an SSD, and why does that matter for something carried in a bag?

questions.q: A company needs to archive 200 TB of records cheaply, and will rarely read them. Which storage is most suitable?
options: Magnetic tape or magnetic hard disks
questions.feedback: Magnetic storage is by far the cheapest per terabyte, and slow access does not matter for an archive.
